reason: `Time.at(now)` builds the stubbed Time; the trails clock method takes a `Temporal.Instant` directly, so there is no `at` constructor to call.

Rails' first `to_time` is the Ruby Date arm's `date_or_time.midnight.to_time`; trails' Date arm takes a JS `Date` (a Ruby Time, not a Ruby Date), so the only `toTime` left is the one after `Time.zone.parse`, which inverts the pair's order.
